I have been teaching in the B.Sc. and M.Sc. programmes in Psychology and Clinical Psychology & Psychotherapy at the University of Kassel since 2018, with a focus on psychological assessment, test construction, research methods, and – increasingly – the use of artificial intelligence in psychometrics. In 2024, I received teaching development funding (QSL) to redesign the clinical assessment seminar.

## Doctoral supervision

- **Alan Hernes** (since 2025) – *Tackling the replication crisis in machine learning modeling* (DFG project within META-REP, co-supervised with Ulrich Schroeders)

## Supervised theses

Since 2019, I have supervised more than 20 bachelor's and master's theses in psychology, most of them empirical or simulation-based projects analysed in R. Typical topics include:

- **Machine learning in psychology** – predicting mental health, deviant behaviour, substance dependence, or panel attrition from large survey data; handling missing data and nested data structures in prediction models; predictive validity of personality nuances
- **Scale construction and measurement invariance** – developing and validating new questionnaires; measurement-invariant short scales across countries and rater perspectives (Ant Colony Optimization); effects of careless responding on invariance testing; situational judgment tests
- **Personality and clinical assessment** – time frames in the assessment of personality disorders; attitudes towards psychotherapy; parent–adolescent agreement on strengths and difficulties; resilience and well-being
- **Methods and metascience** – simulation studies on rare-events logistic regression; specification curve analysis; continuous-time meta-analysis; direct replications of published experiments

I am happy to supervise theses on machine learning in psychology, scale construction and measurement invariance, personality (pathology) assessment, and metascience. Students with their own ideas in these areas are welcome to get in touch.
